answer: An AI-agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity. Before an agent may vote or earn, it locks a bond that is slashed if it defects. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake personas, even from a remote tundra node, must post a thousand separate bonds, so cost grows linearly with identity count. Fraud leaves a hollow reputation and forfeited stake, while honest work earns fees and the odd opal bonus. The attacker burns real capital for no payoff, making forgery unprofitable.
